scope: Read-only review of OAuth decision note and AL-S05 report update. No private app-list access, browser fallback, host/provider/DB calls, code changes, or credential access.
findings: The decision correctly distinguishes legacy client_credentials success from Seller identity proof and keeps the legacy result AUTHENTICATED_UNLINKED. It does not promote a guessed AppID, supplied Client ID, numeric prefix, company fields, or unverified JWT claim into canonical Seller identity.

The discussion of grant-dependent `sub` semantics is explicitly bounded by a separate provider-attested identity-proof requirement. It does not assert that decoding a JWT is sufficient or that a token claim alone is accepted without validation.

The authorization-code path is described as a future candidate requiring app registration, callback, seller consent, scope and protocol qualification. PKCE support is marked unknown/not asserted, not claimed as supported or unsupported.

The owner-provided Swagger method accepting caller-supplied orgId and returning vendor_tag is correctly treated as no Seller crosswalk. The decision does not claim the source document or token exchange proves cabinet ownership.

The AL-S05 update is consistent with the decision: Performance remains unlinked, owner-supplied Swagger remains OWNER_SUPPLIED_REVIEWED rather than automatically fresh, no code/service/DB/key change is claimed, and AL-S05 stays open.

The private-app inventory was not inspected because the originating browser context was unavailable. The note records that limitation and asks only for existing app name/settings editability or absence; it does not ask for new credentials or authorize callback registration.
remaining_gate: Wait for the owner-reported existence/name/settings-access fact for an existing private Ozon app. Then qualify an official provider-attested identity mapping and scopes before proposing source/package implementation. Until that proof exists, retain AUTHENTICATED_UNLINKED and do not combine Seller and advertising reports.
